propositions: Current fixed-count threshold (compact.threshold=10) causes retained snapshot bytes to grow superlinearly Θ(N²) as ticket state grows, reaching 344× amplification at N=8,000 events.

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence with trigger pending_source_bytes >= alpha * active_snapshot_bytes bounds retained snapshots to Θ(N) with tunable amplification factor ≈ 1/alpha while keeping replayed bytes within alpha × snapshot size.

All three cadence candidates (fixed-count control, geometric, byte-cost) preserve ADR 0035 invariants: conservative horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, mixed-version rollback, and two-clone union safety, since they modify only the WHEN trigger, not snapshot placement or retire/restore logic.

Geometric cadence achieves Θ(N) storage but allows unbounded replay tail (2,880 events at N=8,000); byte-cost variant binds read cost to (1+alpha)× of unavoidable snapshot load, making it the preferred candidate for growing state.

Recommended implementation requires new config knob compact.snapshot_alpha (default ≤0 for backward-compat), ADR authoring, and decomposition into separate implementation ticket; no production code change is authorized in this research phase.
